policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: The variant adds only the article τὴν before περίχωρον; ASV 'all the region round about the Jordan' needs the definite English article either way, so the wording does not distinguish presence or absence of the Greek article.

ASV moves straight from 'Isaiah the prophet' into the quotation with no rendering of λέγοντος ('saying'), which the longer reading would supply; the ASV renders λέγων where it stands in this chapter (3:16 'saying unto them all'), so its absence here reflects the shorter text.
εὐθείαν and εὐθείας differ only in number of the predicate noun; ASV 'the crooked shall become straight' uses an uninflected adjective that renders either singular or plural.
Deliberative subjunctive ποιήσωμεν and future ποιήσομεν are both rendered by English 'must we do'; ASV 'What then must we do?' shows no feature that fixes the mood.
ASV reports the reply in the past, 'And he answered and said unto them', matching the imperfect ἔλεγεν; the ASV renders the present λέγει as 'saith', so the past tense here reflects the imperfect.
Subjunctive ποιήσωμεν and future ποιήσομεν are alike rendered 'must we do'; ASV 'Teacher, what must we do?' does not distinguish the mood.

ASV 'And we, what must we do?' fronts the emphatic pronoun as the transposed reading does, but English requires the pronoun before the interrogative clause in any case, and 'must we do' fits subjunctive and future alike; neither word order nor mood is settled. The greek_gloss note concerns 'soldiers', not this unit.
Dative αὐτοῖς and πρὸς αὐτούς are both rendered 'unto them'; ASV 'And he said unto them' does not distinguish them.

The readings differ in word order and in πᾶσιν against ἅπασιν, both 'all'; ASV 'John answered, saying unto them all' renders either, and English clause order is not diagnostic. The notes here gloss 'worthy' and the preposition, not this unit.

ASV has the infinitive 'thoroughly to cleanse his threshing-floor', parallel with 'to gather', which renders διακαθᾶραι; the future indicative διακαθαριεῖ (with or without καί) would give 'and he will thoroughly cleanse'.
ASV 'and to gather the wheat into his garner' is an infinitive coordinate with 'to cleanse', rendering συναγαγεῖν, not the future συναξεῖ ('and he will gather').
ASV 'added this also to them all' renders the adverbial καί with 'also'; the reading that omits καί leaves nothing for that word.
The variant adds the article τῇ before φυλακῇ; 'in prison' is the idiomatic English for the phrase whether or not the article stands, so the ASV does not distinguish it.
ὡς and ὡσεί are both rendered 'as'; ASV 'as a dove' does not distinguish them.

ASV passes directly from 'a voice came out of heaven' to 'Thou art my beloved Son' with nothing rendering the added λέγουσαν ('saying'); the ASV does render λέγων when it stands in this chapter (3:16), so the omission reflects the shorter text.
The variant adds only the article ὁ with Ἰησοῦς; ASV 'And Jesus himself' renders the name identically with or without the Greek article.

The readings differ only in whether ἀρχόμενος precedes or follows ὡσεὶ ἐτῶν τριάκοντα; ASV 'when he began to teach, was about thirty years of age' must place the temporal clause before the English copula in either case, so the order is not distinguished.

ASV 'being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph' places the parenthesis after 'the son', excluding the transposed ὡς ἐνομίζετο υἱός, which would give 'as was supposed, the son of Joseph'. The two remaining readings differ only in the printed comma, which the ASV parenthesis renders either way.
ASV transliterates 'the son of Josech', which renders Ἰωσήχ; Ἰωσήφ would give 'Joseph'.
ASV reads 'the son of Jesus', rendering Ἰησοῦ; Ἰωσή would give 'Jose'.
ASV prints 'the son of Salmon' in the text, which renders Σαλμών, and relegates the other reading to the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities write Sala.'

ASV names both 'Amminadab' and 'Arni', and only this reading carries that pair; the reading beginning Ἀδμὶν τοῦ Ἀρνί lacks Amminadab, and Ἀμιναδάβ τοῦ Ἀράμ is put aside by the mapped note 'Some ancient authorities write Aram.' The other mapped note, 'Many ancient authorities insert the son of Admin', marks Admin as unrendered in the ASV text while leaving this the only reading its two printed names permit.
